title: Cadet Deck and Priority Tuning - All Hands
topics: Culture: async docs and meeting hygiene
summary: Company all-hands focused on Q4 priority tuning: balancing growth projects vs. reliability investments. Leadership presented a compact set of asks for squads, clarified runway for Dedicated and Private pushes, and committed to two cross-functional pilots. Open Q&A covered on-prem pricing, SOC2 timeline, and hiring pace.

People Ops to share hiring projection and interview panel changes by 2026-10-30

Ava Patel: Publish prioritized roadmap PDF and link to squads by 2026-10-28

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-25
Start time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees (selected): Maya Singh, Liam Chen, Ava Patel, Diego Rivera, Sofia Martinez, all hands

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
Leadership walked through Q4 'trimmed priorities' exercise; emphasized shipping high-confidence optimizations (batching, cache improvements) and delaying a small number of exploratory experiments. Announced two pilots: a Dedicated throughput pilot with three customers and an internal Private deployment run to validate KMS/HSM flows. Questions about SOC 2 timing and on-prem pricing; leadership asked squads to adopt a two-week stabilization window before feature flags are widened.

Topics covered: Q4 priorities, hiring and hiring freezes, SLAs and product tradeoffs, incident template, cross-functional pilots, meeting hygiene.

Transcript (timestamps are approximate):
[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone um thanks for joining on time um we wanted to keep this tight today, 55 minutes ish, a lot to go through so i'll run quick through the deck and then open it up for q and a 
[00:00:12] Maya: just a reminder, this is the cadet deck and priority tuning session, so think of it as "what's in scope for the next 90 days and what's getting trimmed" 
[00:00:26] Liam: quick housekeeping, recorded and notes in the all-hands folder, if you spot anything missing flag it in the doc, uh Sofia will follow up on meeting notes cadence 
[00:00:35] Sofia: yep i'll post a summary and the new meeting hygiene template after this call 
[00:00:42] Ava: ok slide one, small set of bullet points, mission aligned items top: 1) reliability and SLOs 2) Dedicated commercial ramp 3) Private deployment readiness and compliance 4) reduce unit cost through batching and caching improvements 
[00:00:59] Ava: we're trimming exploratory fairness evals and the big generative multimodal hackathon into a smaller experiment pool for now, to keep focus on ship and stabilize 
[00:01:12] Diego: to add, eng capacity is not infinite, so we'll protect the reliability work first — that includes KV cache improvements and kernel selection work that Liam's team has been owning 
[00:01:25] Liam: quick note, some of the kernel selector experiments are showing good perf on p4/awd? -- sorry, misread, p4/amd type setups, but we need more perf data on long-seq workloads before we fully flip them on 
[00:01:43] Audience (Engineer 1): are we keeping the Dedicated pricing promo for three pilot customers? 
[00:01:49] Maya: yes, three customers for a rotational pilot, it's a narrow promo tied to feedback and perf numbers, not a mass discount, we want real telemetry before scaling 
[00:02:02] Liam: and technically, we'll route pilot traffic through a canary path in the smart routing layer so failures can be rolled back quickly 
[00:02:12] Ava: product ask: squads to adopt "two-week stabilization window" after feature flags for any runtime or routing changes — essentially a pause before widening exposure 
[00:02:25] Diego: for reliability incidents, new incident template is live — please use the incident doc {link} when you're triaging, it captures KV cache, batch sizes, and kernel paths for us to reproduce 
[00:02:41] Speaker 3: small note, the incident doc link has a typo in the index, i'll open a PR after the meeting 
[00:02:48] Sofia: thanks, quick HR/hiring update slide, we are keeping the hiring bar high but opening heads for Production Infra and Observability; timeline is rolling, no company-wide freeze but there's more scrutiny on IC hires right now 
[00:03:05] Maya: want to be transparent, runway is fine, but we are prioritizing capital efficiency; that means some projects we loved will be paused, and some teams will be nudged to reduce scope 
[00:03:19] Audience (Product PM): curious on SOC 2 posture — are we still aiming for early next year? 
[00:03:25] Liam: yes SOC 2 Type II still on track for Q1 next year, the auditor kickoff is scheduled and Security is on top of remedys — note: timeline depends on a couple missing evidence items so please route any docs requests quickly 
[00:03:40] Maya: also want to call out Private (VPC/on-prem) push, we have two internal pilots to validate KMS/HSM rotations and audit logs, that'll help product and sales answer enterprise questions faster 
[00:03:56] Diego: technical detail: for on-prem we will ship a trimmed installer with a private control plane and provide a hardened set of kernels; the goal is to avoid feature mismatch with hosted as much as we can 
[00:04:09] Audience (Sales rep): on pricing for Private customers, are we standardizing a base + usage model or still bespoke? 
[00:04:16] Maya: short answer: base + usage for most, bespoke for heavily regulated or large deployments; Sales will get a pricing playbook — we'll share it with field by next week 
[00:04:29] Ava: next slide, Optimize — cost/perf toolkit — we are focusing on three levers: intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and quant profiles; we will defer the bigger auto-quantization product until after the pilots 
[00:04:44] Liam: from infra ops, continuous batching improvements already shave 8-12% in token cost on average in our internal benchmarks, but long-tail latencies need work 
[00:04:55] Maya: ok quick time check, then we'll move into q and a, if you have a backlog question drop it in chat and we'll triage during the q and a segment 

Q&A segment:
[00:05:10] Audience (Data Scientist): any change to model catalog curation? we've had customers ask for more verified smaller models for cost-sensitive apps 
[00:05:18] Ava: yes we'll add a "cost tier" filter to the catalog and highlight verified performance profiles; expect that in the next sprint 
[00:05:27] Audience (Support): SLA language — will we commit to specific latency numbers for hosted vs dedicated? 
[00:05:33] Liam: hosted will keep best-effort, Dedicated will have SLA targets, the playbook will include what happens on breach (fallbacks to lower-capacity model variants, credits, or retries) 
[00:05:45] Audience (Engineer 2): can we get more clarity on the smart routing fallbacks you mentioned? i heard something about auto-fallback to quantized model variants? 
[00:05:53] Diego: yes that's right, the routing policy can fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained, including lower-precision quant profiles; we need to be careful about quality regressions so each fallback will have an associated eval set 
[00:06:09] Speaker 2: (mumbled) how often do we run those evals? 
[00:06:12] Ava: cadence will be tied to rollout, but for critical fallbacks we'll run daily small-sample checks and weekly full-eval runs 
[00:06:21] Audience (Legal): any change to audit logs retention for Private installs? some customers want longer retention windows 
[00:06:27] Maya: retention is configurable in Private, for hosted we have default retention periods but offer addons for longer retention 
[00:06:35] Audience (Sales): procurement process question — are we standardizing legal terms for Dedicated? we keep getting re-negotiation requests 
[00:06:41] Maya: Legal is working on a more standard template for Dedicated with a few toggles; Treasury is also aligning billing terms to reduce cycles 

Midpoint note (roughly 20 minutes in): leadership ran through metrics briefly — latency percentiles, token cost curve, net new paying customers this quarter, and churn. There was an interruption with an audio glitch; transcript may miss 30-45 seconds around 00:22 due to dropouts.

[00:07:05] Liam: tech highlight, kernel selector improvements: the new path reduces cuda memory blowups on long sequences, we saw a 15% reduction in OOMs on internal tests but need more customer traffic to be confident 
[00:07:22] Diego: also batch sizing autotuner is now in staging, it learns favored sizes for each model and route, it can reduce individual token latency variance 
[00:07:35] Audience (Engineer 3): can you remind folks on the cache eviction policy? i've seen some expiry interactions with prefix caching 
[00:07:41] Liam: eviction is LRU-ish plus TTL for prefix caches; we added a hook to surface eviction stats into the Console so squads can tune TTLs per workflow 
[00:07:54] Sofia: console update — new per-route dashboards will land next week, they show token-level cost, latency p50/p95/p99, and top error classes 
[00:08:06] Audience (PM): will the dashboards include per-customer cost breakouts? 
[00:08:10] Ava: yes per-route and per-customer rollups for customer owning teams; privacy and access controls via RBAC will limit who can see which accounts 

Open floor questions and some quick wins called out:
[00:08:30] Audience (IC): suggestion: small hack — add a "quiet hours" label to the calendar so meetings get fewer recurring holds during focus blocks 
[00:08:36] Maya: love it, Sofia can we prototype? 
[00:08:40] Sofia: yes will push a template and calendar labels by the end of the week 

Incident retrospective snippet:
[00:09:00] Diego: short postmortem summary for the recent degraded latency incident: root cause was a batcher deadlock on a particular model variant when seq len spiked; fix was to add a watchdog and split the batch queue into two sized-lanes; long term we want improved observability on queueing and per-kernel metrics 
[00:09:23] Audience (SRE): did we update runbooks to call out the new watchdog thresholds? 
[00:09:27] Diego: yes runbook updated, link in the incident doc 

People Ops and hiring Q&A:
[00:09:40] Sofia: hiring update — opening five net new roles this quarter focused mostly in infra, product, and security; interview panels will be smaller and faster, we aim to reduce time-to-offer by 20% 
[00:09:53] Audience (IC): are we changing compensation bands? 
[00:09:56] Maya: no immediate changes to bands, we are reviewing equity vesting cadence but that's not final yet — People Ops will share details soon 

Cross-functional pilots announcement:
[00:10:10] Ava: two pilots: 1) Dedicated throughput pilot with three customers (commercial + perf feedback) 2) Private install pilot to validate KMS/HSM rotations and audit logs with one regulated partner; both are timeboxed and will drive product decisions for Q1 
[00:10:27] Maya: pilots are small and instrumented; we'll publish a telemetry checklist and expected feedback cadence for participating teams 

Audience and misc questions (rapid fire):
[00:10:40] Audience (Sales): will we make the pricing playbook public internally? 
[00:10:44] Maya: yes internal playbook, field only, not public docs 
[00:10:47] Audience (Engineer 4): any policy on deprecating old model variants? 
[00:10:51] Liam: deprecation policy will include a deprecation window, migration guide, and auto-fallback path — we'll aim for a 60-90 day deprecation window for most variants 

Wrap and recap:
[00:11:05] Maya: ok bullets to recap — we trimmed non-essential bets, protect reliability work, two pilots launching, SOC2 timeline on track, dedicated pricing playbook to be shared, hiring is selective but open in key squads; action items will be posted and owners will follow up 
[00:11:25] Maya: final ask — squads, please adopt the two-week stabilization window and ensure runbooks are updated before wide rollout 
[00:11:33] Ava: product will publish the trimmed roadmap and the three metrics we will all watch (latency p95, unit token cost, onboarding time for Dedicated) 
[00:11:45] Diego: eng will share the reliability checklist and the incident runbook update link
[00:11:52] Sofia: people ops will share the hiring panel update and the meeting hygiene template 

Closing micro-Q&A and handoffs (remaining time used for follow-ups):
[00:12:05] Audience (IC, quiet): question about the bench size for infra hires? but this is better for the people ops thread so i'll drop it there 
[00:12:12] Maya: great, post it in #people-ops and we'll respond there 

(There was a short audio dropout around [00:22:10] that clipped about 30 seconds; some lines near that timestamp are estimated by the automated system)

[00:12:30] Maya: thanks everyone, we know this is a lot of change, but the frame here is focus and ship with confidence; small teams with clear metrics win this quarter 
[00:12:41] Liam: quick tech PS — if you need perf traces, use the new trace service and add the tag 'all-hands-demo' so it's easier to find 
[00:12:50] Ava: and i'll post the slide deck, the trimmed roadmap PDF, and the prioritized OKR list right after this meeting 
[00:13:00] Maya: ok meeting adjourned, we'll follow up in threads, thanks all
